title: distributed-credit-reclaimer-and-usage-historicalizer
creator: Ayesha Kapoor
description:
Background: We continue to see edge cases where late-arriving token events, transient gateway retries, and cross-region fanout cause over-crediting or temporary mismatches between the real-time meter and the canonical billing ledger. This work creates a resilient background pipeline that (1) replays raw event streams into a canonical historical store with strong idempotency and multi-pass correction semantics, and (2) runs a distributed reclaim/compensation job that issues offset credits or reclaims provisional credits for customers when reconciling late-arrival differences.

Goals:
- Produce a durable, queryable historicalized consumption store (cold-tier) that preserves event provenance, original request metadata, and reconciliation deltas.
- Implement an idempotent "replayer" that can be run continuously and as an ad-hoc backfill to correct downstream aggregations without double-counting.
- Implement a reclaim/compensation orchestrator that calculates net deltas and emits credits or debit adjustments to the billing ledger with audit records.
- Ensure every adjustment is reversible and traceable for compliance / audit.

Success metrics:
- <5 per-100k billing adjustments after 90 days (measured as post-invoice corrections).
- Backfill throughput >= 10M token events/hour for a single bounded window (parallelized across 8 workers).
- End-to-end reconciliation latency for common late-arrival patterns reduced from ~36 hours to <6 hours.

Scope and non-goals:
- Includes connectors from ingestion topics (kafka/ingest-shards) and the creation of a versioned, append-only historical store in object storage + index.
- Includes the compensation job that writes adjustments to the ledger-sink (idempotent writes with fencing).
- Out of scope: billing UI changes, invoice generation changes, or customer-facing credit presentation (handled by PM as follow-up).

High-level approach:
1) Historicalization: capture raw token events with original request headers, route metadata, and provenance tags into a compact Parquet daily partitioned dataset (s3). Maintain an event index in Postgres for fast lookup by request_id and window watermark.
2) Idempotent Replayer: design worker that reads historical partitions and emits normalized events into the reconciliation staging topic. Each emitted record carries an event_fingerprint and a monotonic sequence to allow at-least-once to become effectively once. Use a write-once prefix in the staging topic keyed by (tenant_id, event_fingerprint).
3) Compensation/Adjustment Orchestrator: windowed aggregation compares canonical ledger state to reconstructed consumption for windows. When delta exceeds epsilon, emit a compensation operation: {type: CREDIT|DEBIT, amount_tokens, reason_code, trace_links}. Compensation writes go through the same ledger-sink with a fencing token to avoid duplicate application.
4) Safeguards and human-in-the-loop: for deltas > threshold (configurable per-tenant), pause automatic application and create a review ticket with pre-populated evidence (link to Parquet partition, sample events, sample carrier).

Dataflow diagram (textual):
kafka.ingest -> raw-event-lambda (enrichment) -> event-archive (s3/parquet) -> replayer-workers -> reconciliation-staging-topic -> reconciliation-aggregator -> compensation-orchestrator -> ledger-sink -> billing-ledger

Key design decisions and trade-offs:
- Cold store format: Parquet chosen for cost and columnar scan efficiency. We accepted slightly higher backfill complexity vs. using a row store.
- Indexing: maintain a lightweight Postgres index for request_id -> s3-partition mapping for fast sampling; avoid storing full payloads in Postgres to limit RTO/RPO risk.
- Idempotency strategy: prefer deterministic event_fingerprint (sha256 of canonicalized event) + per-tenant write-once keys in staging topic. This avoids central locking at the cost of extra storage and fingerprint computation.
acceptance_criteria: Historical Parquet partitions exist for the last 30 days and are queryable via the data platform (athena/great-expectations checks).
Replayer can run a backfill of a 24h window and finish within 3 hours on the provisioned cluster size (8 workers).
Compensation orchestrator emits idempotent ledger adjustments; repeated runs do not create duplicate ledger entries (demonstrated in canary).
Alerting established for mismatch rates and for paused manual-review jobs; dashboards created in Grafana with SLOs.
notes: 2026-03-02: Kickoff discussion — agreed to prefer Parquet cold store over row-store to reduce S3 egress for audits. (Ayesha)
2026-03-04: Prototype replayer produced that fingerprints events and successfully wrote to reconciliation-staging-topic using write-once keys. Benchmark: ~1.5M events/hour/core. (Liam)
2026-03-06: Design review with Security — approved encryption-at-rest + KMS key per-region; recommended additional HMAC on event_fingerprint for tamper evidence. (Security: Nora Patel)
2026-03-08: PM feedback (Diego Morales) — add manual review workflow for top-tier customers and an opt-out flag for automatic compensation. Updated scope accordingly.
2026-03-09: Data team (Ravi Singh) asked to add schema versioning header on Parquet files and integrate with existing provenance registry. Action: add version=1.0 metadata.
runbook: Runbook: 1) If replayer job fails, check worker logs (k8s namespace: billing-replayer) and restart job via k8s job controller. 2) For stuck write-once keys, run the idempotency-checker tool (scripts/idempotency_check.sh) to surface conflicts. 3) If compensation orchestrator pauses due to large delta, run manual_review_collector to generate ticket with evidence; follow the manual review playbook in Confluence. 4) If ledger-sink shows duplicate writes, validate fencing tokens and run ledger-adjudicator to revert duplicates using audit trace.
risks: Large backfills may increase S3 read costs and impact other ETL jobs during peak windows.
Fingerprint collisions — improbable but possible; mitigation: include tenant_id + sequence when computing fingerprint and run nightly collision check.
Operator error during manual compensation could lead to misapplied credits; mitigations: require 2-person review for >$500 credits.
qa_plan: QA plan: 1) Unit tests for fingerprinting and write-once semantics. 2) Integration test that replays synthetic late-arrival events and asserts ledger delta is applied exactly once. 3) Canary: run against a shadow tenant dataset (tenant_shadow_001) and verify no impact to production ledger. 4) Load test: simulate 50M events/day and validate throughput and latency targets.
review_feedback: Design review (2026-03-05) — Ops requested circuit-breaker when compensation error rate >1% for a tenant. Action: implement tenant-level throttles.
Security review (2026-03-06) — add HMAC and per-region KMS; ensure audit logs include operator identity for manual adjustments.
PM review (2026-03-08) — add support for per-tenant auto-apply toggle and manual review queue.
